posts.text:
Adam Smith in Theory of Moral Sentiments said money doesn't equate to happiness. A poor man could find himself wealthy, but still unhappy. Wealth is a tool to produce happiness, but not an end itself. In Wealth of Nations, capitalism would make poor people better off, but only if the rich were restrained by the government through breaking up monopolies. He also said that "joint-stock companies," which is what we today call "corporations" were prone to irresponsibility. That corporations should only be permitted to exist by the state for narrow public purposes and with strict governmental oversight. He believed that high wages for workers was the true measure of a flourishing nation. Not the profits of a powerful investor class with organized capital which would 'trickle down' to the people. He supported confiscatory taxation to prevent extreme hoarding of wealth which was harmful to the wellbeing of regular Englishmen and potentially destabilizing to the nation. He thought wealth should be produced by your labor. Landlords typically do little labor so rent collection was the most unjust form of income. The populace needed a strong education so that they could detect when capitalism started to untether itself from the needs of the nation in order to prevent abuses like corporations offshoring jobs, or importing cheap labor—the very crimes perpetrated by cosmopolitan capitalists against Americans and Europeans for profit. Thus Adam Smith, the father of capitalism and a classical liberal of the 18th century understood human nature better than the vast majority of modern "economists" regardless of whether they're Keynesian inflation apologists or Austrian laisse faire. 

For many years, the Adam Smith Foundation a "conservative" think tank has intentionally misrepresented what he actually believed for libertarian propaganda purposes.

Unbelievably, Iran (yes, Iran) has just been elected to the UN Committee that sets the priorities for women’s rights, counter-terrorism and peacekeeping. This, the country with an almost uniquely violent record of brutalising women, executing peaceful female protesters and of course sponsoring very widespread terrorism.

Equally unbelievably, the UK nominated Iran and although the voting is secret, we must assume it subsequently voted for Iran in the General Assembly. This is the same UK that is nominally run by PM Andy Burnham who declared only a few weeks ago that “we will always stand with the underdog and take what action we can to support them.” 

If the young women of Iran who dare to remove their headscarves, or sing, or engage in peaceful protest to press for basic democracy aren’t the underdog in their battle with a vicious and murderous regime… who then is an underdog? 

I can’t exaggerate how ashamed I am of my country. I’m sickened and repulsed by what it has become. I barely recognise it. Burnham should hang his head in utter shame. 

And as for the UN, it has come to embody institutional corruption and gaslighting on a global scale. 

It put China, Qatar and Cuba in charge of the body charged with protecting human rights worldwide.

It put China, Cuba, Nicaragua, Saudi Arabia, and Sudan (all of which crush/ban NGOs in their own countries) in charge of the body that decides which civil-society groups and NGOs get UN accreditation and access. 

It put Syria (under Assad) in charge the body that promotes education, culture, and press freedom.

How long must this continue? The UN has no credibility whatsoever and should be stripped back to the basics- a debating chamber for the big global issues of the day. And nothing more. 

How can anyone defend this?
